# Comparison with other tools

Assessed **2026-11-25**: 30 dimensions (24 with a verdict, 6 informational), 22 columns (21 other tools and codespec), 660 cells. codespec cells cite its repository at revision [`70c6c4eb`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/tree/70c6c4ebc42c) (version 0.13.0); every other cell cites the page it was read from, read on 2026-11-25.

The assessment is data: [`website/data/comparison.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/website/data/comparison.json), format `codespec-comparison/1`, with its JSON Schema [`schemas/comparison-1.schema.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/schemas/comparison-1.schema.json). `task docs-check` reads the file strictly into the types the schema is generated from, refuses a cell without a source, checks that every cited file and line of this repository exists, checks every "only" below against the cells, and fails when this page differs from what the file renders.

## How to read it

Each cell is one of:

- **yes**: A source says the tool does it, as the dimension defines yes.
- **partial**: A source says the tool does part of it, as the dimension defines partial. Where a reading was ambiguous, the one harder on the tool was taken and the note says so.
- **no**: A source says the tool does not do it, or defines the tool's scope so that it structurally cannot (the note says so then). A page that is silent is not a source for no: that cell is unknown.
- **unknown**: No public source we could read says it. It does not mean no. It has no source.
- **planned**: Assessed tool only: designed or built and not on main. Never counted as yes.
- **info**: The cell is text, not a verdict: the dimension is informational.

**Only**, on this page, means: of the 22 columns of this matrix, on the cells shown, on 2026-11-25. Each statement below about who has **yes** is checked against the cells by `task docs-check`, which fails when the cells give `yes` to another column. An **unknown** cell may hide a capability, so a count of cells is a reading aid and not a score: the dimensions are not equally important.

## Where codespec stands out

1. **Answers that say what they could not see (S3).** codespec is the only column with `yes`: a result carries `definite` or `possible` and the unknown sites that made it possible <sup>[codespec S3](#fn-codespec-s3)</sup>. CodeQL is `no` (global flow drops paths "and no warning is given") <sup>[CodeQL S3](#fn-codeql-s3)</sup>, SCIP and ast-grep are `no` <sup>[SCIP S3](#fn-scip-s3)</sup> <sup>[ast-grep S3](#fn-ast-grep-s3)</sup>; Semgrep, Infer, SpotBugs, Capslock, OpenRewrite and Coccinelle reach `partial` through incompleteness warnings only <sup>[Semgrep CE S3](#fn-semgrep-ce-s3)</sup> <sup>[Infer S3](#fn-infer-s3)</sup> <sup>[SpotBugs S3](#fn-spotbugs-s3)</sup> <sup>[Capslock S3](#fn-capslock-s3)</sup> <sup>[OpenRewrite S3](#fn-openrewrite-s3)</sup> <sup>[Coccinelle S3](#fn-coccinelle-s3)</sup>; the rest are `unknown`.
2. **A conformance kit for third-party adapters (E1).** codespec ships a kit of one case per feature id and a command that gives per-feature verdicts <sup>[codespec E1](#fn-codespec-e1)</sup>. The nearest others are `partial`: test harnesses with no feature vocabulary or verdicts <sup>[Semgrep CE E1](#fn-semgrep-ce-e1)</sup> <sup>[SCIP E1](#fn-scip-e1)</sup> <sup>[staticcheck / go/analysis E1](#fn-go-analysis-e1)</sup>. All others are `unknown`.
3. **Reading one language and writing another from the same model, checked by running both (C4, C5).** codespec is the only column with `yes` on both <sup>[codespec C4](#fn-codespec-c4)</sup> <sup>[codespec C5](#fn-codespec-c5)</sup>. Every other column is `no` or `unknown` on translation <sup>[OpenRewrite C4](#fn-openrewrite-c4)</sup> <sup>[ast-grep C4](#fn-ast-grep-c4)</sup> <sup>[Coccinelle C4](#fn-coccinelle-c4)</sup>.
4. **A written edit is read again and must equal the expected model before it is printed or written (C3).** codespec is `yes` <sup>[codespec C3](#fn-codespec-c3)</sup>. The only other `yes` is Snyk Code, whose engine re-checks each machine-proposed fix inside the vendor's cloud service <sup>[Snyk Code C3](#fn-snyk-code-c3)</sup>; the open codemod tools stop at a test-time comparison or a syntax check <sup>[OpenRewrite C3](#fn-openrewrite-c3)</sup> <sup>[ast-grep C3](#fn-ast-grep-c3)</sup>.
5. **Documented determinism (E2).** codespec states and tests that the same input gives the same bytes <sup>[codespec E2](#fn-codespec-e2)</sup>. Others are at most `partial` (a stated part: <sup>[Clang SA / tidy E2](#fn-clang-sa-e2)</sup> <sup>[staticcheck / go/analysis E2](#fn-go-analysis-e2)</sup> <sup>[Capslock E2](#fn-capslock-e2)</sup>) and Infer documents non-determinism <sup>[Infer E2](#fn-infer-e2)</sup>. The rest are `unknown`.
6. **Refusal with a reason as the policy for unmodelled constructs (S1).** `yes` for codespec <sup>[codespec S1](#fn-codespec-s1)</sup> and for one other, Capslock, which marks unanalysable paths `UNANALYZED` <sup>[Capslock S1](#fn-capslock-s1)</sup>. CodeQL, Semgrep, Joern, Infer and others continue with a diagnostic or an approximation (`partial`) <sup>[CodeQL S1](#fn-codeql-s1)</sup> <sup>[Semgrep CE S1](#fn-semgrep-ce-s1)</sup> <sup>[Joern S1](#fn-joern-s1)</sup> <sup>[Infer S1](#fn-infer-s1)</sup>.
7. **Effects and syscalls per function, with call sites (A3).** `yes` for codespec and Capslock only <sup>[codespec A3](#fn-codespec-a3)</sup> <sup>[Capslock A3](#fn-capslock-a3)</sup>. Both are limited to one ecosystem: codespec's syscall barrier exists for Go on linux/amd64 only <sup>[codespec A3](#fn-codespec-a3)</sup>.
8. **The combination.** One typed model for all readers (L3), one IR for all languages (R1), a documented versioned schema (R2), three-valued answers (S3), user recursion (Q3) and control-flow path queries (Q4) are all `yes` for codespec and for no other column. Joern is next: `yes` on R1, R2 and Q4, `partial` on L3 and Q3, `unknown` on S3 <sup>[Joern R1](#fn-joern-r1)</sup> <sup>[Joern R2](#fn-joern-r2)</sup> <sup>[Joern Q4](#fn-joern-q4)</sup> <sup>[Joern L3](#fn-joern-l3)</sup> <sup>[Joern Q3](#fn-joern-q3)</sup> <sup>[Joern S3](#fn-joern-s3)</sup>. Capslock is `yes` on L3 and S1 and `no` on R1 <sup>[Capslock L3](#fn-capslock-l3)</sup> <sup>[Capslock S1](#fn-capslock-s1)</sup> <sup>[Capslock R1](#fn-capslock-r1)</sup>. The query language is Datalog in the CodeQL and Soufflé tradition <sup>[codespec Q1](#fn-codespec-q1)</sup>; the difference is the typed model and the definite or possible answer.

## Where codespec is behind

1. **Taint (A4).** `planned` <sup>[codespec A4](#fn-codespec-a4)</sup>. `yes` for CodeQL, Semgrep Pro, Joern, Infer, Snyk Code, Doop and Clang SA <sup>[CodeQL A4](#fn-codeql-a4)</sup> <sup>[Semgrep Pro A4](#fn-semgrep-pro-a4)</sup> <sup>[Joern A4](#fn-joern-a4)</sup> <sup>[Infer A4](#fn-infer-a4)</sup> <sup>[Snyk Code A4](#fn-snyk-code-a4)</sup> <sup>[Doop (Soufflé) A4](#fn-doop-a4)</sup> <sup>[Clang SA / tidy A4](#fn-clang-sa-a4)</sup>.
2. **Diff of two revisions (C1).** `planned`: `codespec diff` exists on an open branch, not on `main` <sup>[codespec C1](#fn-codespec-c1)</sup>. Capslock is `yes` today (`-output=compare` against a saved baseline) <sup>[Capslock C1](#fn-capslock-c1)</sup>; Infer, Semgrep, SonarQube and others offer finding-level comparison (`partial`) <sup>[Infer C1](#fn-infer-c1)</sup> <sup>[Semgrep CE C1](#fn-semgrep-ce-c1)</sup> <sup>[SonarQube C1](#fn-sonarqube-c1)</sup>.
3. **SARIF and CI (E6, E5).** codespec prints text and its own JSON formats and has no SARIF <sup>[codespec E6](#fn-codespec-e6)</sup>; CodeQL, Semgrep, Infer, Snyk Code, Doop, SpotBugs, Clang SA and ast-grep list SARIF <sup>[CodeQL E6](#fn-codeql-e6)</sup> <sup>[Semgrep CE E6](#fn-semgrep-ce-e6)</sup> <sup>[Infer E6](#fn-infer-e6)</sup> <sup>[Snyk Code E6](#fn-snyk-code-e6)</sup> <sup>[Doop (Soufflé) E6](#fn-doop-e6)</sup> <sup>[SpotBugs E6](#fn-spotbugs-e6)</sup> <sup>[Clang SA / tidy E6](#fn-clang-sa-e6)</sup> <sup>[ast-grep E6](#fn-ast-grep-e6)</sup>. codespec has exit codes and no published CI integration (`partial`) <sup>[codespec E5](#fn-codespec-e5)</sup>; 14 columns are `yes` on CI, for example <sup>[CodeQL E5](#fn-codeql-e5)</sup> <sup>[Semgrep CE E5](#fn-semgrep-ce-e5)</sup>.
4. **Shipped rules (E7).** The public engine ships 18 built-in checks, and the repository's own record of running them on one public test repository has 8 findings, all false <sup>[codespec E7](#fn-codespec-e7)</sup>. CodeQL, Semgrep, SonarQube, Snyk Code and others maintain large public or vendor catalogues <sup>[CodeQL E7](#fn-codeql-e7)</sup> <sup>[Semgrep CE E7](#fn-semgrep-ce-e7)</sup> <sup>[SonarQube E7](#fn-sonarqube-e7)</sup>.
5. **Language breadth and depth (L1).** codespec reads eight languages, each a subset <sup>[codespec L1](#fn-codespec-l1)</sup>; SonarQube lists 47 <sup>[SonarQube L1](#fn-sonarqube-l1)</sup>, CodeQL 12 <sup>[CodeQL L1](#fn-codeql-l1)</sup>. By the project's own support matrix the Go reader verifies 115 of 121 applicable features and the Rust reader 113, while the Elixir, Gleam and Odin readers verify 30, 25 and 28 (counts of `verified` cells in `website/data/support-matrix.json` at the assessed revision). On real code the Go reader reads a fraction of the standard library's functions: 10.5 % of `syscall`, 28.3 % of `runtime`, 46.8 % of `os` [website/docs/guides/map-a-repository-to-syscalls.md:66-77](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/guides/map-a-repository-to-syscalls.md#L66-L77>).
6. **Dependencies (A6).** `partial`: only Go has a dependency reading path <sup>[codespec A6](#fn-codespec-a6)</sup>. Capslock, Doop and the Go analysis framework are `yes` <sup>[Capslock A6](#fn-capslock-a6)</sup> <sup>[Doop (Soufflé) A6](#fn-doop-a6)</sup> <sup>[staticcheck / go/analysis A6](#fn-go-analysis-a6)</sup>.
7. **Precision of the effect analysis.** Dispatch over the whole standard library is wide: with `cha` most functions that do IO share one large component, and the measured entry point of one library leaves 155 reachable functions `unknown` (66 interface calls, 59 function values, 27 runtime functions) [docs/static-analysis.md:218-226](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/static-analysis.md#L218-L226>). The effect summaries are claims not yet checked against a run [docs/static-analysis.md:235-241](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/static-analysis.md#L235-L241>).
8. **Points-to and pattern authoring.** Points-to analysis beyond dispatch is out of scope [docs/query-language.md:330](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/query-language.md#L330>); Doop is built on it <sup>[Doop (Soufflé) A2](#fn-doop-a2)</sup>. Writing a query by example in source syntax, as Semgrep and ast-grep do, is planned for cq [docs/query-language.md:325](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/query-language.md#L325>), not shipped <sup>[Semgrep CE Q1](#fn-semgrep-ce-q1)</sup> <sup>[ast-grep Q1](#fn-ast-grep-q1)</sup>.

## Caveats

- The dimension list is ours. It follows what codespec does, so it is kind to codespec on change, translation and conformance, which most tools do not try to do, and it leaves out dimensions where other tools lead: IDE integration, hosted dashboards, ticket integration, size of the rule community, breadth of languages with deep semantic analysis.
- The cells about codespec were written by the group that maintains codespec. Check them against the cited lines.
- Several `no` cells for analysis-only tools on C2 to C5 rest on scope pages, not on a statement that the feature is absent. The note of the cell says which.
- Public documentation may lag the code, in both directions. codespec's own pages disagree in two places we found: `docs/conformance.md:3` still says "proposed, not implemented" while the status page, the CLI reference and the kit show it shipped; `docs/static-analysis.md` and `docs/query-language.md:155` say only the Go reader lists calls, while `CHANGELOG.md` records call lists for the Rust and Groovy readers. The cells follow the shipped behaviour in the changelog and the CLI reference.
- API-only tools (go/analysis, SpotBugs, Error Prone, Clang) have no query language; their Q3 is `partial` (recursion in host-language code). Single-language tools are `no` on R1.
- OpenRewrite is assessed as the open-source engine, Semgrep as two columns by tier, SonarQube as the self-managed product with the edition named in a cell where it differs.

## Input

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [L1](#dim-l1) | Languages | The languages the tool analyses or edits, as its own documentation lists them. Cell text: the list or the count. | text, not a verdict |
| [L2](#dim-l2) | Front end | How source is read: compiler front end (type-checked, from the language's own compiler or type checker), build-intercepting extractor (runs the real build), tree-sitter, own parser, bytecode, or an index produced by a compiler. Cell text: the kind. | text, not a verdict |
| [L3](#dim-l3) | Typed model | Every expression of the model the analysis runs on has a resolved type. | **yes**: types resolved for every expression in the supported languages. **partial**: types for some languages or some constructs. **no**: syntax only. |

### Notes and sources

#### L1 Languages {#dim-l1}

- <a id="fn-codespec-l1"></a>**codespec** Reads Go, Rust, Java, Groovy, C, Elixir, Gleam, Odin (each a subset); writes Go, Rust, C, Elixir, Gleam, Odin [website/docs/index.md:16](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/index.md#L16>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-l1"></a>**CodeQL** 12 entries: C/C++, C#, GitHub Actions, Go, Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, TypeScript (versions per page). [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-overview/supported-languages-and-frameworks/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-l1"></a>**Semgrep CE** "30+ Community supported languages" for CE; some languages (for example Apex) are platform-only. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-pro-vs-oss>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-l1"></a>**Semgrep Pro** "35+ supported languages" including Pro-only ones (Apex, C/C++); cross-file dataflow GA for C#, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Python, TypeScript, C/C++. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/supported-languages>)
- <a id="fn-joern-l1"></a>**Joern** C/C++, Java, JavaScript, Python, x86/x64 binaries, JVM bytecode, Kotlin, PHP, Go, Swift, Ruby, C# (12 frontends; maturity varies) [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-l1"></a>**Infer** Pulse page: supported C/C++/ObjC, Hack, Java; experimental Erlang, Rust. About page lists Java, C, C++, Objective-C, Erlang. Release 1.3.0 adds Python, Swift frontends. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-pulse>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-l1"></a>**SonarQube** 47 entries in Server 2026.5 (22 in Community Build): Java, C#, JS/TS, Python, Go, PHP, Rust, C/C++, COBOL, IaC and more. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/overview>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-l1"></a>**Snyk Code** 16 languages: Apex, C/C++, COBOL, Dart/Flutter, Go, Groovy, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript, .NET, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Swift/Obj-C, TypeScript (some Early Access). [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages/supported-languages-package-managers-and-frameworks>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-l1"></a>**Coverity** 21 languages listed: Apex, C/C++, C#, CUDA, Dart, Fortran, Go, Groovy, Java, JavaScript, JSP, Kotlin, Objective-C/C++, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Swift, TypeScript, VB.NET. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/static-analysis-tools-sast/languages-and-frameworks.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-l1"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** Java (JARs, WARs, APKs, Maven coordinates; Android, Java EE); Python single-file TensorFlow shape analysis (Pythia); experimental Dalvik [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-l1"></a>**Glean** Native indexers: C/C++, Hack, Haskell, JavaScript/Flow, Python; via SCIP or LSIF: Rust, Go, TypeScript, Java, Python, Dotnet [github.com](<https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean>)
- <a id="fn-scip-l1"></a>**SCIP** Indexers list Java, Scala, Kotlin, TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, C, C++, Ruby, Python, C#, Visual Basic, Dart, PHP, Debian packaging files. [github.com](<https://github.com/scip-code/scip>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-l1"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** Go only: staticcheck calls itself 'a linter for the Go programming language'; the framework loads Go packages. [staticcheck.dev](<https://staticcheck.dev/docs/>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-l1"></a>**SpotBugs** Java: scans bytecode (class files) from JDK 11 and newer; documented as finding bugs in Java programs. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-l1"></a>**Error Prone** Java: 'a static analysis tool for Java that catches common programming mistakes at compile-time'. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/error-prone>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-l1"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** Static Analyzer: C, C++, Objective-C. clang-tidy: C++ linter, also C, Objective-C and CUDA sources. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangStaticAnalyzer.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-l1"></a>**Capslock** Go only: a capability analysis CLI for Go packages. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-l1"></a>**ast-grep** 28 built-in languages (C, C++, Go, Java, Python, Rust, TS, Kotlin, Swift, Bash and others); custom tree-sitter grammars loadable. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/languages.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-l1"></a>**OpenRewrite** Open source: Java, Kotlin, Groovy plus HCL, JSON, Properties, Protobuf, TOML, XML, YAML (June 2026). JS, Python, C# and others via Moderne. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/reference/supported-languages>)
- <a id="fn-comby-l1"></a>**Comby** About 45 languages with basic parsers (Go, Java, Python, Rust, C/C++, TypeScript and others); generic fallback matcher; custom languages via JSON. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/overview>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-l1"></a>**GritQL** 14 target languages: JS/TS, Python, JSON, CSS, Rust stable; Ruby, PHP beta; Java, HCL, Solidity, Markdown, YAML, Go, SQL alpha. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/target-languages>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-l1"></a>**Coccinelle** C (primary); minimal C++ and IBM C modes in spatch 1.3.2; Rust is a separate prototype tool. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### L2 Front end {#dim-l2}

- <a id="fn-codespec-l2"></a>**codespec** Per language: go/types (Go), javac attributed trees (Java), Groovy 2.4 compiler (Groovy), clang typed AST (C), syn plus own name and type resolution (Rust); readers are separate programs [website/docs/concepts/pipeline.md:32-46](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/pipeline.md#L32-L46>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-l2"></a>**CodeQL** Build-intercepting extractor for compiled languages; extractor on source for interpreted ones; tree-sitter based extractor for Ruby. One extractor per language. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-overview/about-codeql/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-l2"></a>**Semgrep CE** Own parsers (pfff) and tree-sitter grammars, converted to a generic AST; patterns parsed by the same front ends. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/contributing-code>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-l2"></a>**Semgrep Pro** Same front ends as CE (pfff, tree-sitter, generic AST); Pro Engine front ends are not documented separately. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/contributing-code>)
- <a id="fn-joern-l2"></a>**Joern** Own or embedded parsers per language (Eclipse CDT, JavaParser, GraalVM, Soot, IntelliJ PSI, Roslyn, ANTLR), Ghidra for binaries; no build needed [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-l2"></a>**Infer** Build-intercepting extractor: wraps the build, runs clang or javac, translates each compiled file into Infer's own IR (SIL); newer frontends emit Textual. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/infer-workflow>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-l2"></a>**SonarQube** Per-language analyzers: Java via ECJ semantics plus compiled bytecode and classpath; JS/TS via TypeScript compiler; C# wraps the build; C/C++ via compilation database. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/java>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-l2"></a>**Snyk Code** Own parser: source is turned into an event graph; for many frameworks Snyk Code needs only to parse the code. No build step stated. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages-package-managers-and-frameworks/snyk-code-language-support-technical-specifications-and-guidance>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-l2"></a>**Coverity** Build-intercepting extractor: cov-build runs the native compiler command and stores results in an intermediate directory; AST dumpable with cov-manage-emit. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/blog/running-codexm-checker-with-coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-l2"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** Bytecode: Soot-based or WALA-based fact generator (Jimple), experimental Dalvik generator; facts loaded into Soufflé [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/blob/master/docs/documentation.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-l2"></a>**Glean** Indexers per language: clang-based wrapper for C++ (compiler replacement); others from SCIP or LSIF indexes or own tooling [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/indexer/cxx/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-l2"></a>**SCIP** Index produced by a compiler or type checker run as a library by each indexer (compiler pipeline run through semantic analysis, then AST traversal). [sourcegraph.com](<https://sourcegraph.com/docs/code-search/code-navigation/writing_an_indexer>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-l2"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** Compiler front end: go/packages loads and type-checks with go/types; analyzers get typed syntax trees. Staticcheck adds an SSA-form IR. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/packages>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-l2"></a>**SpotBugs** Bytecode: 'can scan bytecode (class files)'. Needs compiled classes plus an auxiliary classpath. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-l2"></a>**Error Prone** Compiler front end: a javac plugin that runs over attributed compilation units of the real compile. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-l2"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** Compiler front end (Clang, LibTooling) driven by compile\_commands.json; scan-build interposes on the real build. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-l2"></a>**Capslock** Compiler front end: golang.org/x/tools go/packages with types and syntax loaded, then SSA program built from it. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/analyzer/load.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-l2"></a>**ast-grep** tree-sitter: docs say it parses code into an AST using tree-sitter; syntax-level only. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/how-ast-grep-works.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-l2"></a>**OpenRewrite** Compiler front end: runs the language's own compiler (javac for Java, TypeScript compiler for TS/JS) and keeps its type data. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/type-attribution>)
- <a id="fn-comby-l2"></a>**Comby** Own generic parser for balanced delimiters, strings and comments; no full parse tree per language. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/overview>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-l2"></a>**GritQL** tree-sitter: "GritQL uses tree-sitter for all language parsers". [github.com](<https://github.com/getgrit/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-l2"></a>**Coccinelle** Own C parser (OCaml) with macro and #ifdef handling and error recovery; Rust prototype uses Rust Analyzer. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### L3 Typed model {#dim-l3}

- <a id="fn-codespec-l3"></a>**codespec** yes: Every expression carries its type, required; a document with an expression without a type is refused [docs/design.md:74](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/design.md#L74>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-l3"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Java schema gives every expression a typeid; dynamic languages (JavaScript, Python, Ruby) are not type-resolved. Partial across languages, so P. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/codeql/main/java/ql/lib/config/semmlecode.dbscheme>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-l3"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: Typed metavariables exist but type support is "shallow": local variables and arguments only, not field accesses or array elements. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/pattern-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-l3"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: Cross-file analysis adds "type inference" across files; docs describe type support as shallow for typed metavariables. Not every expression typed. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-code/semgrep-pro-engine-intro>)
- <a id="fn-joern-l3"></a>**Joern** partial: Java frontend runs a type solver and docs say skipping type inference makes results much worse; other frontends use type recovery, no every-expression guarantee documented [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/frontends/java/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-l3"></a>**Infer** partial: SIL is typed for C-family and Java; Hack and Python frontends are dynamically typed, so not every expression has a resolved type (harder reading). [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-pulse>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-l3"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Java and JS/TS have semantic models (ECJ, TypeScript type-checking); unresolved types possible with missing classes; other languages not documented as typed. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/java>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-l3"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Engine lists type inference and point-to analysis among its analyses; no statement that every expression has a resolved type. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-l3"></a>**Coverity** partial: Structural model combines dependencies, compilers and language semantics; no statement that every expression is typed in every language. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/static-analysis-tools-sast/coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-l3"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** partial: Facts include Var\_Type per variable from Jimple; docs do not claim every expression typed, Python path has no such model documented [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/blob/master/docs/doop-101.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-l3"></a>**Glean** partial: C++ indexer is a clang wrapper; SCIP and LSIF indexers carry whatever types those tools emit; no typed-for-all guarantee documented [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/indexer/cxx/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-l3"></a>**SCIP** no: Index stores symbols, roles and ranges per occurrence, not a type per expression; scope is code navigation (harder reading, indexers type-check internally). [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-l3"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** yes: TypesInfo is 'the result of a complete type-check of the package syntax trees'; packages with type errors are flagged IllTyped. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/packages>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-l3"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: Types inferred from bytecode by type analysis; needs complete auxiliary classpath for hierarchy, otherwise 'not as accurate as possible'. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-l3"></a>**Error Prone** yes: ErrorProneAnalyzer runs 'over attributed compilation units', so javac has resolved types for the trees checks see. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-l3"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: Every Expr has getType(); but template definitions hold dependent nodes, and clang-tidy 'requires valid code to function'. Harder reading: P. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/doxygen/classclang_1_1Expr.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-l3"></a>**Capslock** yes: Load mode requests NeedTypes, NeedSyntax, NeedTypesInfo and NeedDeps; analysis runs on SSA built from type-checked Go packages. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/analyzer/load.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-l3"></a>**ast-grep** no: Works purely at syntax level; lacks type information, control flow, data flow, taint, constant propagation. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/tool-comparison.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-l3"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Types attributed from the compiler for Java-family code with full classpath; Python only "where available"; unresolved types become JavaType.Unknown. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/type-attribution>)
- <a id="fn-comby-l3"></a>**Comby** no: Matching on coarse syntactic structures only; "uses no tree definition" and gives up knowledge of language constructs; no types mentioned. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-l3"></a>**GritQL** no: Parsers are tree-sitter syntax trees; tutorial says each snippet is converted to a syntax tree before matching; no type resolution documented. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/tutorials/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-l3"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: Own C type checker; --type-error-msg shows where it could not determine an expression's type; headers parsed for types. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

## Representation

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [R1](#dim-r1) | One IR across languages | One intermediate representation or fact schema serves all supported languages, so one analysis runs on all. | **yes**: one IR/schema for all. **partial**: one for a family of languages, or a shared core with per-language extensions. **no**: per-language models. |
| [R2](#dim-r2) | Documented, versioned IR schema | The IR or fact schema is a public document with a version identifier. | **yes**: public schema with a version. **partial**: public schema (or library API reference) without a version contract. **no**: internal. |

### Notes and sources

#### R1 One IR across languages {#dim-r1}

- <a id="fn-codespec-r1"></a>**codespec** yes: One cir/1 document per module, one definition for all readers and writers; passes and effects run on it for every language [docs/design.md:20](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/design.md#L20>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-r1"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Per-language database schemas, but shared language-agnostic libraries (dataflow, controlflow, ssa, typetracking) serve all languages. [github.com](<https://github.com/github/codeql/tree/main/shared>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-r1"></a>**Semgrep CE** yes: Contributors convert each language's tree-sitter CST into AST\_generic nodes, one generic AST for all languages. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/adding-a-language>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-r1"></a>**Semgrep Pro** yes: One generic AST for all languages (tree-sitter CST converted to AST\_generic); Pro analyses run on it as far as documented. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/adding-a-language>)
- <a id="fn-joern-r1"></a>**Joern** yes: CPG is "a language-agnostic intermediate graph representation of code"; one schema for all frontends [cpg.joern.io](<https://cpg.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-r1"></a>**Infer** yes: Capture translates files into Infer's own internal intermediate language; Textual lets frontend writers emit SIL, so checkers run across languages. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/infer-workflow>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-r1"></a>**SonarQube** no: Language analyzers are downloaded per detected language; docs describe no shared IR. JS/TS taint engine is described as its own engine. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/discovering/analysis-overview/process-steps>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-r1"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Rules are matched against one event-graph model; documentation does not say the graph is language-independent. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages-package-managers-and-frameworks/snyk-code-language-support-technical-specifications-and-guidance>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-r1"></a>**Coverity** partial: CodeXM is designed to be language-independent; examples load a C/C++ library. A shared IR is not documented. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/blog/write-checkers-codexm.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-r1"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** unknown: The page read does not say it. [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-r1"></a>**Glean** partial: No single schema required: each language has its own detailed schema, with language-neutral views built by deriving facts [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-r1"></a>**SCIP** yes: One protobuf schema, scip.proto, is the shared format for all language indexers. [github.com](<https://github.com/scip-code/scip>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-r1"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** no: Single-language tool, no cross-language IR. Go is the only language; one SSA-form IR (x/tools go/ssa, staticcheck has its own go/ir). No cross-language claim. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-r1"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: One bytecode model for Java classes; documentation names Java only. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-r1"></a>**Error Prone** no: Single-language tool, no cross-language IR. javac syntax trees for Java only; no cross-language IR. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/installation>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-r1"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: One Clang AST for the C family of languages (C, C++, Objective-C); no wider shared IR. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangStaticAnalyzer.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-r1"></a>**Capslock** no: Single language (Go); one SSA program from x/tools, no cross-language IR. Harder reading of a multi-language dimension. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-r1"></a>**ast-grep** no: One rule cannot target several languages: similar languages have different parsing trees; models are per-grammar tree-sitter trees. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-r1"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Per-language LSTs and visitors (JavaVisitor, YamlVisitor) over shared tree and marker core; no single cross-language IR. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/visitors>)
- <a id="fn-comby-r1"></a>**Comby** partial: One generic matcher parameterised per language by delimiters, strings and comments; no IR or fact schema, only a shared core with per-language syntax tables. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/advanced-usage>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-r1"></a>**GritQL** no: Queries are per target language: a pattern file declares one language and AST node names follow that language's grammar. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/target-languages>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-r1"></a>**Coccinelle** no: C front end and SmPL for C; Rust support is a separate tool with its own front end and no control-flow reasoning. [rust-for-linux.com](<https://rust-for-linux.com/coccinelle-for-rust>)

#### R2 Documented, versioned IR schema {#dim-r2}

- <a id="fn-codespec-r2"></a>**codespec** yes: JSON Schema generated from the Rust model; format id cir/1; a change in meaning is a new version cir/2; feature vocabulary in schemas/cir-1.features.json [website/docs/vision.md:35](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/vision.md#L35>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-r2"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Per-language .dbscheme files are public in the repository; the file carries no version identifier; compatibility handled by database upgrade. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-overview/codeql-glossary/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-r2"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: AST\_generic is public source (libs/ast\_generic) with no documented schema or version contract; only the JSON output has a versioned schema. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/contributing-code>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-r2"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: AST\_generic is public source in the open engine with no documented schema or version contract; Pro internals are proprietary. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/contributing-code>)
- <a id="fn-joern-r2"></a>**Joern** yes: Public specification titled Code Property Graph Specification 1.1; META\_DATA VERSION must be set to "1.1"; no compatibility policy stated [cpg.joern.io](<https://cpg.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-r2"></a>**Infer** partial: Textual parser and grammar sources are public but no README or format version exists; OCaml module API reference is published, no version contract. [github.com](<https://github.com/facebook/infer/tree/main/infer/src/textual>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-r2"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Java plugin API has a versioned changelog; no public schema of the analysis facts or IR found. Harder reading chosen. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/java>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-r2"></a>**Snyk Code** unknown: Event graph described only as an analogy; no schema or version page found.
- <a id="fn-coverity-r2"></a>**Coverity** unknown: Public vendor pages read give no IR or emit schema document. Full guides did not render.
- <a id="fn-doop-r2"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** partial: Fact schema is public as Soufflé declarations in souffle-logic/facts; no version identifier or contract found [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/tree/master/souffle-logic/facts>)
- <a id="fn-glean-r2"></a>**Glean** yes: Public schema sources in glean/schema/source; predicates carry version suffixes (graphql.1), SchemaId hash, evolves directive; docs call versions a legacy feature [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/schema/changing/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-r2"></a>**SCIP** partial: scip.proto is public; ProtocolVersion enum defines only UnspecifiedProtocolVersion, so no concrete version number; backwards compatibility is promised in prose. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/scip.proto>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-r2"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** partial: Public API reference for go/ssa and gob-encoded facts, but the module is pre-v1 ('Stable version' unmet); no version contract for the IR. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-r2"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: Detector API (BytecodeScanningDetector, OpcodeStackDetector) is public; no versioned IR schema. Result XML has a separate XSD. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/implement-plugin.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-r2"></a>**Error Prone** partial: Public Javadoc for the check API (BugChecker, VisitorState, dataflow package); no versioned schema or stability contract found. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-r2"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: AST API is public (doxygen, AST matcher reference) with no version contract: matchers 'will change along with the changes in the clang AST'. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/QueryBasedCustomChecks.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-r2"></a>**Capslock** partial: Output schema capability.proto is public, proto2, no version field; docs say capability names and mappings are not stable before 1.0. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/docs/capabilities.md>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-r2"></a>**ast-grep** partial: Node API documented (SgNode, kinds) but marked experimental, no schema versioning scheme; Rust API not stable. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/api.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-r2"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: LST types documented informally for Java with source links to a release tag; no schema version contract or compatibility statement. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/lst-examples>)
- <a id="fn-comby-r2"></a>**Comby** no: FAQ: Comby "uses no tree definition", tree only implicit in the parser; exporting a parse tree "isn't implemented". [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-r2"></a>**GritQL** unknown: No public versioned schema of the syntax trees found in the GritQL docs read; node names come from tree-sitter grammars.
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-r2"></a>**Coccinelle** unknown: Debug flags print internal types (--cocci-internals); no public versioned IR schema found.

## Soundness

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [S1](#dim-s1) | Policy on a construct it cannot model | What happens at a construct outside the model. | **yes**: refuse or mark unknown, with a reason and a position, kept in the output. **partial**: warn or diagnose but continue with an approximation. **no**: approximate silently, or documentation does not say and the design is heuristic. |
| [S2](#dim-s2) | Coverage measured and reported | The tool reports, per run, how much of the code it read or analysed (files, functions, lines, extraction success). | **yes**: a per-run coverage figure or report. **partial**: only error or warning counts, or partial. **no**: none. |
| [S3](#dim-s3) | Absent versus unseen | A query or finding distinguishes 'not found' from 'could not see' (three-valued or possible/definite answers). | **yes**: documented. **partial**: partial (for example only an incompleteness warning). **no**: none. |

### Notes and sources

#### S1 Policy on a construct it cannot model {#dim-s1}

- <a id="fn-codespec-s1"></a>**codespec** yes: A construct a reader cannot express is kept verbatim as a foreign statement with a reason, listed as a refusal; an unsummarised call is unknown, never pure [docs/static-analysis.md:35-37](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/static-analysis.md#L35-L37>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-s1"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Extraction errors and warnings go to a log; analysis continues. Docs call a few extractor errors healthy; no per-construct unknown marker. [docs.github.com](<https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/troubleshooting-code-scanning/extraction-errors-in-the-database>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-s1"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: Parse or internal errors mark a target skipped with path and reason (analysis\_failed\_parser\_or\_internal\_error); scan continues with the rest. [github.com](<https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-interfaces/blob/main/semgrep_output_v1.jsonschema>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-s1"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: Parse or internal errors mark a target skipped with path and reason; Pro findings can be tagged PRO\_REQUIRED; scan continues. [github.com](<https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-interfaces/blob/main/semgrep_output_v1.jsonschema>)
- <a id="fn-joern-s1"></a>**Joern** partial: UNKNOWN node catches AST nodes with no suitable node type and records PARSER\_TYPE\_NAME; no refusal policy or report documented [cpg.joern.io](<https://cpg.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-s1"></a>**Infer** partial: Pulse makes optimistic assumptions about unknown calls and scrambles reachable state; skipped calls appear only in debug summaries, may cause false negatives and positives. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-pulse>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-s1"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Missing classes give a warning and placeholder symbols; unknown symbols are flagged via isUnknown(); analysis continues with approximation. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/java>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-s1"></a>**Snyk Code** no: Partially supported frameworks give possible false negatives; AI-based heuristic engine; no per-run reason or position for unmodelled constructs documented. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages-package-managers-and-frameworks/snyk-code-language-support-technical-specifications-and-guidance>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-s1"></a>**Coverity** unknown: Public pages read do not state a policy; the documentation site body did not render.
- <a id="fn-doop-s1"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** partial: Opaque methods are excluded from normal invocation handling by documented ad-hoc rules; legacy engine may not handle lambdas or proxies; no per-run report [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plast-lab/doop/master/souffle-logic/facts/opaque-methods.dl>)
- <a id="fn-glean-s1"></a>**Glean** unknown: The page read does not say it. [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-s1"></a>**SCIP** unknown: The protocol defines no policy for unmodelled constructs; it is left to each indexer, none documented centrally.
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-s1"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** partial: Parse and type errors are recorded per package in Errors, not failing Load; callers 'may need to handle such errors'. Nothing for other constructs. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/packages>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-s1"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: Unfound referenced classes are listed when analysis completes and analysis continues with less precision; no position per construct. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-s1"></a>**Error Prone** unknown: Docs read give no policy for constructs outside the model.
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-s1"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: Calls it cannot see into are evaluated 'conservatively (as if no definition were available)'; clang-tidy refuses invalid code with clang-diagnostic-error. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/developer-docs/IPA.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-s1"></a>**Capslock** yes: Cgo, assembly, linkname calls get CGO or ARBITRARY\_EXECUTION; unanalysable call paths get UNANALYZED; reflect and unsafe pointer reported as capabilities, with call paths. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/docs/caveats.md>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-s1"></a>**ast-grep** no: Docs say tree-sitter recovers from syntax errors and continues parsing; no per-construct unknown marker documented (harder reading). [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-s1"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Unresolved types become the JavaType.Unknown sentinel; parse failures throw only if throwOnParseFailures is set (default false). [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/reference/gradle-plugin-configuration>)
- <a id="fn-comby-s1"></a>**Comby** no: Designed to be "more robust to matching patterns in the presence of unrecognized constructs"; unsupported languages fall to a generic matcher without a diagnostic. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-s1"></a>**GritQL** no: Docs do not say how files that fail to parse are handled; design is tree-sitter based matching (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/tutorials/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-s1"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: Parser skips a function that does not parse and resumes at the next; errors shown with --parse-error-msg; not kept in output by default. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### S2 Coverage measured and reported {#dim-s2}

- <a id="fn-codespec-s2"></a>**codespec** yes: codespec measure prints read and refused functions per file and the share read; left\_out names the denominator (test-only code); support matrix per feature and language [website/docs/reference/cli.md:132-134](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/reference/cli.md#L132-L134>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-s2"></a>**CodeQL** partial: CLI prints baseline lines of code; GitHub tool status page shows percent of files scanned and per-file extraction status. No CLI coverage report. [docs.github.com](<https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/managing-your-code-scanning-configuration/about-the-tool-status-page>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-s2"></a>**Semgrep CE** yes: Scan summary prints "Targets scanned" and "Parsed lines: \~100%"; JSON lists paths.scanned and (verbose) paths.skipped. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/getting-started/quickstart-ce>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-s2"></a>**Semgrep Pro** yes: Same scan summary and JSON paths.scanned and skipped as CE; interfile\_languages\_used reported (platform JSON). [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-appsec-platform/json-and-sarif>)
- <a id="fn-joern-s2"></a>**Joern** unknown: The page read does not say it. [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-s2"></a>**Infer** partial: Option --log-pulse-coverage logs where coverage stops in stats/stats.txt; stats directories exist. No per-run coverage figure by default. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/man/next/infer.1.html>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-s2"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Warnings for inaccessible classes; C/C++ taint logs a warning and is skipped when its quality index is too low. No per-run coverage figure documented. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/c-family/customizing-the-analysis>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-s2"></a>**Snyk Code** unknown: No per-run coverage report found in Snyk Code documentation read.
- <a id="fn-coverity-s2"></a>**Coverity** yes: cov-analyze prints a summary per run including Files analyzed. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/blog/running-codexm-checker-with-coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-s2"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** unknown: The page read does not say it. [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-s2"></a>**Glean** unknown: The page read does not say it. [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-s2"></a>**SCIP** partial: scip stats outputs statistics about an index and scip lint flags issues; no per-run coverage of source read is documented. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/CLI.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-s2"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** unknown: No per-run coverage figure found in framework or staticcheck docs read.
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-s2"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: XML has FindBugsSummary (total\_classes, total\_size, num\_packages) and Errors missingClasses; the schema does not define them as coverage. [github.com](<https://github.com/spotbugs/spotbugs/blob/master/spotbugs/etc/bugcollection.xsd>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-s2"></a>**Error Prone** unknown: No per-run coverage figure found in the docs read.
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-s2"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: Per-entry-point statistics CSV (dump-entry-point-stats-to-csv) and -analyzer-stats counters; no stated coverage percentage. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/developer-docs/Statistics.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-s2"></a>**Capslock** partial: Flag -noisy includes output on unanalyzed function calls; no per-run coverage figure of packages or functions read. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/cmd/capslock/capslock.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-s2"></a>**ast-grep** unknown: Scan and JSON output pages list matches and severity only; no per-run coverage figure documented.
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-s2"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Only optional logging of compilation warnings and errors and parse-failure exceptions; no per-run coverage figure documented. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/reference/gradle-plugin-configuration>)
- <a id="fn-comby-s2"></a>**Comby** unknown: No per-run coverage figure in pages read (CLI, API and FAQ pages).
- <a id="fn-gritql-s2"></a>**GritQL** unknown: No per-run coverage figure documented in CLI reference.
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-s2"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: --parse-c reports parse errors per file, --verbose-match reports functions skipped for lacking required patterns; no coverage figure. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### S3 Absent versus unseen {#dim-s3}

- <a id="fn-codespec-s3"></a>**codespec** yes: A finding or row carries certainty definite or possible with the unknown sites that made it possible; a negation across unread code is possible [docs/query-language.md:158-161](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/query-language.md#L158-L161>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-s3"></a>**CodeQL** no: Global flow drops paths over the access-path limit "and no warning is given"; no documented not-found versus could-not-see answer. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/analyzing-data-flow-in-java/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-s3"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: Only incompleteness signals: partial-scan and skip reasons in the output; no three-valued or possible/definite findings. [github.com](<https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-interfaces/blob/main/semgrep_output_v1.jsonschema>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-s3"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: Findings carry engine\_kind and PRO\_REQUIRED pro\_feature flags (interproc\_taint, interfile\_taint); only incompleteness signals, no three-valued answers. [github.com](<https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-interfaces/blob/main/semgrep_output_v1.jsonschema>)
- <a id="fn-joern-s3"></a>**Joern** unknown: The page read does not say it. [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-s3"></a>**Infer** partial: Pulse separates latent from manifest issues and records skipped\_calls per summary; no documented not-found versus could-not-see answer. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-pulse>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-s3"></a>**SonarQube** unknown: No page found on three-valued or possible/definite results.
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-s3"></a>**Snyk Code** unknown: No page found on distinguishing not found from could not see.
- <a id="fn-coverity-s3"></a>**Coverity** unknown: No readable page on distinguishing not found from could not see.
- <a id="fn-doop-s3"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** unknown: The page read does not say it. [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-s3"></a>**Glean** unknown: The page read does not say it. [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-s3"></a>**SCIP** no: Protocol is a transmission format for navigation data, "not meant as a storage format for querying"; no query answers, so no three-valued result. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-s3"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** unknown: No documented distinction between not found and could not see; staticcheck docs state only a low-false-positive goal.
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-s3"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: Only an incompleteness message listing missing classes; findings are not marked possible or definite. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-s3"></a>**Error Prone** unknown: No documented distinction between not found and could not see.
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-s3"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** unknown: No documented three-valued or possible/definite result found in the docs read.
- <a id="fn-capslock-s3"></a>**Capslock** partial: UNANALYZED capability marks call paths the tool could not analyze; no three-valued answer, and data-race writes through interfaces are not reported. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/docs/capabilities.md>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-s3"></a>**ast-grep** no: Matching is purely structural on syntax trees; no three-valued or could-not-see answers; FAQ lists no semantic analysis (harder reading). [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-s3"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Unresolved types are marked JavaType.Unknown and tests flag missing types; no three-valued query answers documented. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/reference/type-attribution>)
- <a id="fn-comby-s3"></a>**Comby** unknown: No three-valued or could-not-see answers documented in pages read.
- <a id="fn-gritql-s3"></a>**GritQL** unknown: No distinction of not found versus could not see documented.
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-s3"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: --partial-match and --verbose-match report partial or skipped matches; --steps warns a rule may fail by running out of steps. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

## Query

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Q1](#dim-q1) | Query style | The form of a user-written query: Datalog-like, object-oriented query language, pattern by example, graph traversal DSL, API (library code), rule configuration only, none. Cell text: the form. | text, not a verdict |
| [Q2](#dim-q2) | User-authored rules | Users can write their own checks or queries. | **yes**: documented, supported way. **partial**: possible only through a library API or by forking. **no**: it does not. |
| [Q3](#dim-q3) | Recursion in user queries | The query language supports recursion (transitive closure) written by the user. | **yes**: it does. **partial**: through built-in closure operators only. **no**: it does not. |
| [Q4](#dim-q4) | Control-flow paths in queries | A query can ask about paths in the control-flow graph: 'on every path', 'before/after', dominance. | **yes**: documented. **partial**: partial (for example path-insensitive 'ellipsis' matching or built-in checks only). **no**: it does not. |
