### Notes and sources

#### Q1 Query style {#dim-q1}

- <a id="fn-codespec-q1"></a>**codespec** cq: typed Datalog with named-field record patterns, stratified negation, aggregates, path patterns and typestate properties [docs/query-language.md:47-56](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/query-language.md#L47-L56>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-q1"></a>**CodeQL** Object-oriented query language QL (declarative, logic-based): from/where/select with classes and predicates. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-overview/about-codeql/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-q1"></a>**Semgrep CE** Pattern by example: code-like patterns with ellipsis and metavariables, composed in YAML rules; taint mode via source, sink, sanitizer patterns. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/pattern-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-q1"></a>**Semgrep Pro** Pattern by example in YAML rules; taint mode with sources, sinks, sanitizers, and Pro-only propagators. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/data-flow/taint-mode/overview>)
- <a id="fn-joern-q1"></a>**Joern** Scala-embedded traversal DSL (CPGQL, steps over the code property graph) run in a REPL, scripts or server; also QueryDB Query.make objects [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/cpgql/reference-card/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-q1"></a>**Infer** Topl: user state-machine property files; Pulse taint: JSON source, sink, policy config; annotation-reachability flags; custom checkers as OCaml code (Infer.AI). [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-topl>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-q1"></a>**SonarQube** Java plugin API (library code); XPath 1.0 over the AST in the web UI for Flex, PL/SQL, PL/I, XML; generic issue import. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/extension-guide/adding-coding-rules>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-q1"></a>**Snyk Code** Rule configuration only: Rule Extensions register sanitizer functions by fully qualified name in the web UI or REST API. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-fix-and-prevent/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code/rule-extensions/configure-rule-extensions>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-q1"></a>**Coverity** CodeXM: functional domain-specific language, expression-based; loops over global sets, filters with patterns and a which-are operator. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/blog/write-checkers-codexm.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-q1"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** Datalog (Soufflé dialect) rules, run with --extra-logic or as standalone Soufflé files over the facts and CSV results [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/blob/master/docs/doop-101.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-q1"></a>**Glean** Angle: declarative logic language similar to Datalog, with negation (!), if/then/else, arrays and sets; non-recursive [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/angle/guide/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-q1"></a>**SCIP** None: SCIP is data; consumers write code against the Go, Rust, TypeScript and Haskell bindings or generated protobuf code. [github.com](<https://github.com/scip-code/scip>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-q1"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** API (library code): an Analyzer value with a Run function written in Go. Staticcheck: configuration of checks only, no query form. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-q1"></a>**SpotBugs** API (Java detector plugin with findbugs.xml registration); XML filter files only select or suppress bugs. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/implement-plugin.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-q1"></a>**Error Prone** API (Java BugChecker with matchers) plus Refaster before/after templates (pattern by example); flags only select severity. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/plugins>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-q1"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** API (C++ AST matchers and checker classes, in-tree); clang-tidy also has experimental clang-query custom checks and a YAML taint config. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/Contributing.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-q1"></a>**Capslock** None: fixed capability classification; only a custom capability map file (-capability\_map) and -capabilities filter. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/cmd/capslock/capslock.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-q1"></a>**ast-grep** Pattern by example (code with $META variables) plus YAML rule objects with relational and composite rules. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/rule.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-q1"></a>**OpenRewrite** API (library code): Java visitors over the LST, declarative YAML recipes composing other recipes, Refaster templates, JavaTemplate snippets. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/recipes>)
- <a id="fn-comby-q1"></a>**Comby** Pattern by example with holes (:\[x\], :\[\[x\]\], :\[x:e\]) plus where-rules (equality, match, rewrite, regex). [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/syntax-reference>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-q1"></a>**GritQL** Pattern by example: code snippets with $metavariables, AST node patterns, where clauses and logic clauses (and, or, not, contains, within, until). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/syntax>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-q1"></a>**Coccinelle** Semantic patch language SmPL: C-like patch with -/+ lines, metavariables, dots over control-flow paths, rule dependencies, Python/OCaml scripts. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### Q2 User-authored rules {#dim-q2}

- <a id="fn-codespec-q2"></a>**codespec** yes: codespec query -f runs a user's cq module; codespec check --names replaces name lists; codespec edit runs user edit programs [website/docs/reference/cli.md:217-232](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/reference/cli.md#L217-L232>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-q2"></a>**CodeQL** yes: Custom .ql queries documented; run with the CLI, shipped in query packs. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/writing-codeql-queries/about-codeql-queries/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-q2"></a>**Semgrep CE** yes: Users write own YAML rules ("rules you write yourself"); rule syntax documented. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/rule-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-q2"></a>**Semgrep Pro** yes: Custom rules supported with the same rule syntax; Pro features such as interfile: true enabled per rule. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/rule-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-joern-q2"></a>**Joern** yes: Custom steps via Scala implicit classes, QueryDB queries and plugins are documented [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/cpgql/custom-defined-steps/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-q2"></a>**Infer** yes: Topl documents user-written temporal properties; Pulse taint config takes user JSON sources, sinks, sanitizers, policies. Topl is experimental. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-topl>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-q2"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Custom rules through plugin API for Java, PHP, Python, COBOL, RPG; XPath rules for four languages; other languages only import external reports. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/extension-guide/adding-coding-rules>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-q2"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Enterprise-only Rule Extensions add custom sanitizers to existing rules; writing new detection rules not found (older custom-rules pages could not be read). [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-fix-and-prevent/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code/rule-extensions>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-q2"></a>**Coverity** yes: CodeXM lets users create customized checkers; run with cov-analyze --codexm. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/blog/write-checkers-codexm.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-q2"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** yes: Doop 101 documents extra rules during the analysis (--extra-logic) and standalone Soufflé queries over result files after it [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/blob/master/docs/doop-101.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-q2"></a>**Glean** yes: Users write own schemas, queries and derived predicates; Angle documented for building linters, migration and refactoring tools [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-q2"></a>**SCIP** partial: Only through library API: bindings let users write own consumers; the format itself offers no checks or queries. [github.com](<https://github.com/scip-code/scip>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-q2"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** yes: Framework decides: declare an Analyzer, run it with singlechecker, multichecker or go vet -vettool. Staticcheck docs read show no custom-check mechanism. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-q2"></a>**SpotBugs** yes: Documented: 'Implement SpotBugs plugin' with Maven archetype, detector base classes, test harness and registration files. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/implement-plugin.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-q2"></a>**Error Prone** yes: Documented: plugin checks written 'exactly the same way as the built-in checks', loaded from the annotation processor path via ServiceLoader. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/plugins>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-q2"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** yes: clang-tidy decides: documented way to write checks with AST matchers, plus experimental query-based custom checks. Analyzer checkers are in-tree only per its manual. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/Contributing.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-q2"></a>**Capslock** partial: Users can supply a custom capability map file mapping functions to capabilities; this is configuration, not user-written queries. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/cmd/capslock/capslock.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-q2"></a>**ast-grep** yes: Custom lint rules in YAML (id, language, rule, constraints, fix), tested with ast-grep test. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/project/lint-rule.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-q2"></a>**OpenRewrite** yes: Authors write imperative (Java visitor), declarative (YAML) and Refaster recipes; documented, with RewriteTest for testing. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/recipes>)
- <a id="fn-comby-q2"></a>**Comby** yes: User-written match and rewrite templates with optional rules; many patterns per TOML configuration file. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/configuration>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-q2"></a>**GritQL** yes: Users define named patterns, predicates and functions in .grit files or grit.yaml, tested with grit patterns test. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/guides/patterns>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-q2"></a>**Coccinelle** yes: Users write SmPL semantic patches and script rules; documented grammar with examples. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### Q3 Recursion in user queries {#dim-q3}

- <a id="fn-codespec-q3"></a>**codespec** yes: Recursion is part of the language; a depth-limited recursion is accepted when a comparison bounds the step, other unbounded value-making recursion is refused [CHANGELOG.md:42-47](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/CHANGELOG.md#L42-L47>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-q3"></a>**CodeQL** yes: "QL provides strong support for recursion"; user-written recursive predicates plus + and \* closure operators. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/ql-language-reference/recursion/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-q3"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: No user-written recursion; only built-in deep-expression operator matches recursively in subexpressions. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/pattern-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-q3"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: No user-written recursion; only built-in deep-expression operator matches recursively in subexpressions. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/pattern-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-joern-q3"></a>**Joern** partial: Built-in repeat/until/emit/maxDepth operators; harder reading taken, user recursion would be plain Scala outside the documented query language [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/cpgql/repeat-steps/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-q3"></a>**Infer** no: Topl properties are nondeterministic automata with registers; page documents no recursion or transitive closure operator for users. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-topl>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-q3"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Only XPath 1.0 over the AST (built-in axes) or plugin code; no user-written recursive query language documented. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/extension-guide/adding-coding-rules>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-q3"></a>**Snyk Code** no: Only sanitizer registration is documented; no user query language (scope defined by the Rule Extensions page). [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-fix-and-prevent/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code/rule-extensions>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-q3"></a>**Coverity** unknown: CodeXM reference not readable; recursion not confirmed.
- <a id="fn-doop-q3"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** yes: Rules can be recursive; legacy example builds transitive closure on CallGraphEdge; Soufflé tutorial shows reachable(x,z) :- edge(x,y), reachable(y,z). Engine Soufflé decides [souffle-lang.github.io](<https://souffle-lang.github.io/tutorial>)
- <a id="fn-glean-q3"></a>**Glean** no: Introduction: "currently Angle is limited to non-recursive queries only"; recursion work is an open upstream pull request, not released [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-q3"></a>**SCIP** no: Design states SCIP is not a storage format for querying; query engines are left to consumers, so no query language exists. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-q3"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** partial: API tool: recursion only in host-language code, no query language. No query language: analyzers are Go code, so recursion is the host language's. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-q3"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: API tool: recursion only in host-language code, no query language. No query language: detectors are Java code, so recursion is the host language's. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/implement-plugin.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-q3"></a>**Error Prone** partial: API tool: recursion only in host-language code, no query language. No query language: checks are Java code, so recursion is the host language's. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/plugins>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-q3"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: API tool: recursion only in host-language code, no query language. Checks are C++ code, so recursion is the host language's; query-based custom checks have only built-in closure matchers. Read as Y. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/Contributing.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-q3"></a>**Capslock** no: No query language: Capslock is a CLI that reports capabilities reachable through calls, configured by flags only. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-q3"></a>**ast-grep** yes: Utility rules may self-reference inside relational components (has/inside); cycles through composite rules are forbidden. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/rule-config/utility-rule.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-q3"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: No query language; recursion only inside Java visitor code, where traversal is depth-first and authors call super.visitX (harder reading). [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/visitors>)
- <a id="fn-comby-q3"></a>**Comby** no: Rewrite statements cannot be nested ("not currently possible"); match expressions nest but no user recursion or closure documented (harder reading). [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/advanced-usage>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-q3"></a>**GritQL** partial: contains traverses downwards through the syntax tree (built-in); docs do not say whether patterns can call themselves (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/modifiers>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-q3"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: Nests \<... ...\> repeat a pattern zero or more times along paths (built-in); no user-defined recursion documented. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### Q4 Control-flow paths in queries {#dim-q4}

- <a id="fn-codespec-q4"></a>**codespec** yes: path(A -\> B, over: cfg, avoid: ...), every\_path(...), cfg\_next, dominates, postdominates, guards; properties as automata over body or call paths (up to 3 registers) [docs/query-language.md:126-129](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/query-language.md#L126-L129>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-q4"></a>**CodeQL** yes: ControlFlowNode and BasicBlock classes support reachability, "reach B without going through A", and dominance queries (Python guide; other languages similar). [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/analyzing-control-flow-in-python/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-q4"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: Ellipsis matches statement sequences but "does not jump from inner to outer statement blocks"; pattern-inside; no dominance or all-paths operator. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/pattern-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-q4"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: Ellipsis and pattern-inside only; ellipsis "does not jump from inner to outer statement blocks"; no dominance or all-paths operator. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/pattern-syntax>)
- <a id="fn-joern-q4"></a>**Joern** yes: Documents controls, controlledBy, dominates, dominatedBy, postDominates, postDominatedBy as control-flow graph traversals [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/cpgql/control-flow-steps/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-q4"></a>**Infer** partial: Topl automata express ordered method-call sequences over paths, with reachability condition X \~\~\> Y; experimental, no dominance or all-paths operators documented. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-topl>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-q4"></a>**SonarQube** partial: No user-facing control-flow query; built-in flow-sensitive symbolic execution and taint rules only (C/C++ page: context-, flow-, field-sensitive). [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/c-family/understanding-the-analysis>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-q4"></a>**Snyk Code** no: Only sanitizer registration is documented; no path or control-flow query (scope defined by the Rule Extensions page). [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-fix-and-prevent/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code/rule-extensions>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-q4"></a>**Coverity** unknown: CodeXM reference not readable; path queries not confirmed.
- <a id="fn-doop-q4"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** unknown: The page read does not say it. [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-q4"></a>**Glean** unknown: The page read does not say it. [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-q4"></a>**SCIP** no: No query language; design avoids graph encoding, and the schema carries no control-flow graph. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-q4"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** yes: go/ssa blocks have Idom, Dominees and Dominates over the CFG; ctrlflow gives a CFG per function. Used from analyzer code, not a query language. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-q4"></a>**SpotBugs** unknown: Manual documents operand-stack scanning for detectors; no documented CFG path or dominance queries.
- <a id="fn-errorprone-q4"></a>**Error Prone** partial: API exposes dataflow over a control-flow graph (DataFlow.Result pairs an Analysis with a ControlFlowGraph); no path query language. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/dataflow/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-q4"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** yes: Analyzer decides: checkers run path-sensitive over every explored path with CFG; debug checkers dump CFG and dominators. Not a query language. [clang-analyzer.llvm.org](<https://clang-analyzer.llvm.org/checker_dev_manual.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-q4"></a>**Capslock** no: No query language; analysis is a call-graph search from capability nodes, with no control-flow path queries. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-q4"></a>**ast-grep** no: FAQ: no control flow analysis; composition is boolean logic over syntax tree. Only syntactic inside/follows/precedes. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-q4"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Archived Apache-2.0 rewrite-analysis offers control-flow and data-flow utilities and visitors; maintainers advise against new use. [github.com](<https://github.com/openrewrite/rewrite-analysis>)
- <a id="fn-comby-q4"></a>**Comby** no: Scope is "coarse syntactic structures"; no control-flow graph or path queries in the syntax, rules or API pages. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-q4"></a>**GritQL** no: Modifiers walk the syntax tree (contains, within, until) or adjacent siblings (before, after); no control-flow graph in docs read. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/modifiers>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-q4"></a>**Coccinelle** yes: Dots match along control-flow paths with when != and exists/forall; foundation is CTL model checking (POPL 2009). [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

## Analysis

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [A1](#dim-a1) | Interprocedural analysis | Analysis follows calls across function boundaries through a call graph. | **yes**: built-in. **partial**: limited (for example one file, or one level). **no**: intraprocedural only. |
| [A2](#dim-a2) | Dynamic-dispatch resolution | Calls through interfaces or function values are resolved by a documented algorithm (CHA, RTA, points-to, or equivalent). | **yes**: documented algorithm. **partial**: heuristic or limited. **no**: not resolved. |
| [A3](#dim-a3) | Effects and syscalls | Reports what a function may do outside its own memory (file system, network, process, environment, syscalls) as a result of the analysis. | **yes**: built-in effect or capability report per function. **partial**: only through user-written queries or source/sink models. **no**: it does not. |
| [A4](#dim-a4) | Taint tracking | Tracks data from sources to sinks. | **yes**: built-in interprocedural taint. **partial**: intraprocedural or file-local, or limited to some languages or a paid tier. **no**: it does not. |
| [A5](#dim-a5) | Scope of one run | Per file, per compilation unit or project, or whole program including libraries. Cell text: the scope. | text, not a verdict |
| [A6](#dim-a6) | Third-party dependencies | Dependencies are analysed in the same graph as the project. | **yes**: dependency source or bytecode read and analysed with the project. **partial**: summaries or models of libraries, or vulnerability matching on versions only. **no**: it does not. |

### Notes and sources

#### A1 Interprocedural analysis {#dim-a1}

- <a id="fn-codespec-a1"></a>**codespec** yes: Effects and syscalls carried to a fixed point over one call graph of every function of the linked set, SCCs by iterative Tarjan [website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md:104-106](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md#L104-L106>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-a1"></a>**CodeQL** yes: Global data flow tracks "throughout the entire program"; local flow is confined to one callable. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/analyzing-data-flow-in-java/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-a1"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: CE limits: "Single function taint analysis"; constant propagation across functions only within one file. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-pro-vs-oss>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-a1"></a>**Semgrep Pro** yes: Default cross-function analysis within a file; optional cross-file analysis (--pro) for a subset of languages; falls back to single-file after 5 GB or 3 hours. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-code/semgrep-pro-engine-intro>)
- <a id="fn-joern-a1"></a>**Joern** yes: Data-flow engine follows calls; external methods without semantics pass taint from all arguments to all arguments and return value [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/dataflow-semantics/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-a1"></a>**Infer** yes: Pulse is an interprocedural memory safety analysis; compositional per-procedure summaries are applied at call sites. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-pulse>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-a1"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Java symbolic execution is cross-procedural only for non-overridable methods in the same file; taint rules (paid editions) work across files. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/java>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-a1"></a>**Snyk Code** yes: Interfile analysis is available for all supported languages except COBOL. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages/supported-languages-package-managers-and-frameworks>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-a1"></a>**Coverity** yes: Analyses entire codebases across files and libraries for defects spanning components; analysis computes a callgraph. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/static-analysis-tools-sast/coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-a1"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** yes: Whole-program points-to; values flow "via calls and returns"; taint computed inside the points-to machinery [yanniss.github.io](<https://yanniss.github.io/ptaint-oopsla17-prelim.pdf>)
- <a id="fn-glean-a1"></a>**Glean** no: Reading harder: Glean stores facts that indexers produce, including calls and call hierarchies, and runs no call-graph analysis itself [github.com](<https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean>)
- <a id="fn-scip-a1"></a>**SCIP** no: Scope is code navigation (definitions, references, implementations); no call-graph analysis is part of the protocol. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-a1"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** partial: Per-package design: an analyzer 'must not assume that the whole program is available'; dependencies reach it only as facts. ctrlflow noReturn spans one package. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-a1"></a>**SpotBugs** yes: Effort 'more' (default) adds 'interprocedural analysis for application classes'; 'max' extends it to referenced non-application classes. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/effort.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-a1"></a>**Error Prone** no: Dataflow is scoped to the enclosing method, lambda or initializer; each initializer is analysed separately. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/dataflow/DataFlow.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-a1"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** yes: Analyzer decides: inlining of callees creates CallEnter nodes; modes none, basic-inlining, inlining, dynamic, dynamic-bifurcate. clang-tidy checks are per-AST. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/developer-docs/IPA.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-a1"></a>**Capslock** yes: Follows transitive calls to privileged standard library operations through a call graph, backwards from capability nodes. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-a1"></a>**ast-grep** no: FAQ says no scope, type, control-flow, data-flow analysis; matching is per syntax tree. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-a1"></a>**OpenRewrite** no: Call-graph and interprocedural analysis sit in Moderne program analysis (proprietary tier); open-source column has only the archived rewrite-analysis. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/licensing/openrewrite-licensing>)
- <a id="fn-comby-a1"></a>**Comby** no: Matches syntactic structures in text; no call graph or semantic analysis; FAQ describes it as for coarse syntactic structures. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-a1"></a>**GritQL** no: Matching is syntactic on one syntax tree per file; no call graph documented (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/tutorials/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-a1"></a>**Coccinelle** no: SmPL grammar: matching is intraprocedural only; dots never cross into called functions or the next function. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### A2 Dynamic-dispatch resolution {#dim-a2}

- <a id="fn-codespec-a2"></a>**codespec** yes: --dispatch cha (class-hierarchy) or rta (rapid type analysis from the entries); a call with no candidate is unknown; no points-to analysis (out of scope) [website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md:108-119](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md#L108-L119>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-a2"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Java polyCalls approximates overriding targets; docs name no algorithm (no CHA, RTA, points-to) and call reflection "very hard"; function values not covered. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/navigating-the-call-graph/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-a2"></a>**Semgrep CE** unknown: No documented call-resolution algorithm for interfaces or function values found.
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-a2"></a>**Semgrep Pro** unknown: No documented call-resolution algorithm for interfaces or function values; page does not mention dispatch or call graph.
- <a id="fn-joern-a2"></a>**Joern** yes: DynamicCallLinker computes call targets over inheritance hierarchy (class-hierarchy based, credited to SAFEDISPATCH) and adds CALL edges [github.com](<https://github.com/joernio/joern/blob/master/joern-cli/frontends/x2cpg/src/main/scala/io/joern/x2cpg/passes/callgraph/DynamicCallLinker.scala>)
- <a id="fn-infer-a2"></a>**Infer** unknown: No documentation page found naming a dispatch-resolution algorithm for Pulse virtual calls.
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-a2"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Java: behaviours of overridable methods are approximated. JS/TS taint resolves calls during abstract interpretation. No CHA, RTA or points-to algorithm named. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/java>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-a2"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Engine lists point-to analysis; no resolution algorithm (CHA, RTA, points-to variant) is documented. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-a2"></a>**Coverity** unknown: Call-resolution algorithm not documented on readable public pages.
- <a id="fn-doop-a2"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** yes: method-resolution.dl "Encodes a CHA callgraph"; call graph also built on the fly by the points-to analyses (CallGraphEdge) [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plast-lab/doop/master/souffle-logic/basic/method-resolution.dl>)
- <a id="fn-glean-a2"></a>**Glean** no: Same reading as A1: no resolution algorithm in the engine; targets come from the indexer's facts [github.com](<https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean>)
- <a id="fn-scip-a2"></a>**SCIP** no: Scope is navigation; schema has is\_implementation relationships supplied by indexers, with no resolution algorithm documented. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/scip.proto>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-a2"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** partial: go/callgraph offers CHA, RTA and VTA as libraries an analyzer may call; the VTA package says its interface is experimental. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/callgraph>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-a2"></a>**SpotBugs** unknown: No dispatch-resolution algorithm found in the manual pages read.
- <a id="fn-errorprone-a2"></a>**Error Prone** unknown: No dispatch-resolution algorithm found in the docs read.
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-a2"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** yes: Devirtualisation uses path-sensitive DynamicTypeInfo and CallEvent getRuntimeDefinition; mayHaveOtherDefinitions flags uncertainty; dynamic-bifurcate is the default. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/developer-docs/IPA.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-a2"></a>**Capslock** yes: Call graph built with vta.CallGraph (variable type analysis) over all SSA functions; caveats note interface types may include ones absent in practice. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/analyzer/util.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-a2"></a>**ast-grep** no: No type information or semantic analysis, so calls through interfaces or function values are not resolved. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/tool-comparison.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-a2"></a>**OpenRewrite** no: Dispatch approximation by declared type is documented only for Moderne program analysis (proprietary tier); not in the open-source engine. [docs.moderne.io](<https://docs.moderne.io/openrewrite-advanced-program-analysis/advanced-analysis-techniques/>)
- <a id="fn-comby-a2"></a>**Comby** no: No type information or call resolution; syntactic matcher only. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-a2"></a>**GritQL** no: No type model, so calls through interfaces cannot be resolved; matching is syntactic (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/tutorials/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-a2"></a>**Coccinelle** no: Matching is intraprocedural; no call resolution through function pointers or interfaces documented. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### A3 Effects and syscalls {#dim-a3}

- <a id="fn-codespec-a3"></a>**codespec** yes: codespec effects: per function effects (env, fs.read, fs.write, io, net, proc, rand, stdin, stdout, time, db) and syscalls with the call site; syscall barrier exists for Go linux/amd64 only [website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md:148-171](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md#L148-L171>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-a3"></a>**CodeQL** partial: No per-function effect report; sources, sinks and threat models (file, env, stdin, network) are modelled data used by user or built-in queries. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/customizing-library-models-for-java-and-kotlin/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-a3"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: No effect report; sources and sinks are written by rule authors as patterns. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/data-flow/taint-mode/overview>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-a3"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: No effect report; sources and sinks are written as patterns in rules. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/data-flow/taint-mode/overview>)
- <a id="fn-joern-a3"></a>**Joern** partial: No per-function effect report; users query calls to sinks or insecure functions (for example strcpy) with queries or semantics [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/scan/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-a3"></a>**Infer** partial: Annotation-reachability finds methods that directly or indirectly call annotated methods; user-defined source and sink annotations or regex models; no built-in per-function effect report. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-annotation-reachability>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-a3"></a>**SonarQube** unknown: No page found on a per-function effect or syscall report.
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-a3"></a>**Snyk Code** unknown: No page found on a per-function effect or syscall report.
- <a id="fn-coverity-a3"></a>**Coverity** unknown: No readable page on a per-function effect or syscall report.
- <a id="fn-doop-a3"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** partial: Only source/sink/transform lists for taint plus --scan-native-code for JNI calls; no per-method effect report [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/blob/master/docs/ptaint.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-a3"></a>**Glean** no: Same reading as A1: a fact store; no effect report documented [github.com](<https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean>)
- <a id="fn-scip-a3"></a>**SCIP** no: Scope is code navigation, not effect analysis; schema has no effect or syscall fields. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/scip.proto>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-a3"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** unknown: No effect or syscall report found in framework or staticcheck docs read.
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-a3"></a>**SpotBugs** unknown: No per-function effect or syscall report found in the manual pages read.
- <a id="fn-errorprone-a3"></a>**Error Prone** unknown: No effect or syscall report found in the docs read.
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-a3"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: Checkers model file, stream and unix API calls (unix, security packages) and report misuse; no per-function effect report. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/checkers.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-a3"></a>**Capslock** yes: Core purpose: reports capabilities such as FILES, NETWORK, EXEC, SYSTEM\_CALLS, READ\_SYSTEM\_STATE a package or function can reach. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/docs/capabilities.md>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-a3"></a>**ast-grep** no: Syntax-level tool; no semantic or effect analysis; only user patterns could match call names textually. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/tool-comparison.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-a3"></a>**OpenRewrite** unknown: No built-in effect report found in fetched pages; method search recipe page could not be read.
- <a id="fn-comby-a3"></a>**Comby** no: Syntactic matcher with no semantic model; effects could only be found by user patterns on text. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-a3"></a>**GritQL** no: Syntactic query language with no effect model documented (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/tutorials/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-a3"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: No built-in effect report; users write semantic patches that match calls, with scripts to report; examples include NULL dereference checks. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### A4 Taint tracking {#dim-a4}

- <a id="fn-codespec-a4"></a>**codespec** planned: Taint from source to sink along the linked graph is listed as later work (story taint-flows); no taint command ships. Def-use and control-flow relations exist in cq [docs/static-analysis.md:195](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/docs/static-analysis.md#L195>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-a4"></a>**CodeQL** yes: Built-in TaintTracking::Global with source, sink, barrier configuration; RemoteFlowSource predefined. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/analyzing-data-flow-in-java/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-a4"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: Taint mode is intraprocedural in CE; interprocedural taint is "a Semgrep Pro feature" and custom propagators are Pro-only. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/data-flow/taint-mode/overview>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-a4"></a>**Semgrep Pro** yes: Interprocedural taint: --pro-intrafile across functions in a file for nearly all languages; --pro across files for a subset of languages. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/data-flow/taint-mode/overview>)
- <a id="fn-joern-a4"></a>**Joern** yes: Tracks "the propagation of attacker-controlled data" statically; reachableBy and reachableByFlows from sources to sinks [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-a4"></a>**Infer** yes: Pulse taint takes source, sanitizer, sink and policy config via --pulse-taint-config; interprocedural through Pulse summaries. Default config shipped for Java. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/man/next/infer-analyze.1.html>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-a4"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Security-injection (taint) rules show source-to-sink flows, up to 20 per issue; run only in Server and Cloud, not Community Build; languages vary. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/quality-standards-administration/managing-rules/security-related-rules>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-a4"></a>**Snyk Code** yes: Data flow follows data from source to sink; with learned sources, sinks and sanitizers it enables taint analysis, interfile. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-a4"></a>**Coverity** partial: Vendor blog: tainted data tracked from a Struts entry point to sinks via custom framework support; built-in taint checker list not readable. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/blog/remote-code-execution-apache-roller-via-ognl-injection.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-a4"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** yes: P/Taint, enabled with --information-flow, runs inside the points-to analysis; Android and Servlet supported out of the box [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop/blob/master/docs/ptaint.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-a4"></a>**Glean** no: Same reading as A1: scope is "collecting, deriving and working with facts about source code", no taint engine [github.com](<https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean>)
- <a id="fn-scip-a4"></a>**SCIP** no: Scope is code navigation; schema has no data-flow or taint concepts. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/scip.proto>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-a4"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** unknown: No built-in taint tracking found in framework or staticcheck docs read.
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-a4"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: Core: detectors such as FindSqlInjection use data flow. Full taint only via the separate Find Security Bugs plugin (LGPL, configured source/sink files). [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/detectors.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-a4"></a>**Error Prone** unknown: No built-in taint tracking found in the docs read.
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-a4"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** yes: Opt-in optin.taint.GenericTaint on the TaintPropagation modeling checker; built-in sources, sinks, propagation; YAML config not stable; no default filters. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/user-docs/TaintAnalysisConfiguration.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-a4"></a>**Capslock** no: Scope is capabilities reachable by calls; no source-to-sink data flow tracking is described. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-a4"></a>**ast-grep** no: FAQ: "NO" to taint analysis and tracing user input flow; points to Semgrep for taint mode. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-a4"></a>**OpenRewrite** no: Data-flow and security analysis recipes are listed under the Moderne Proprietary License; archived open-source rewrite-analysis does not mention taint. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/licensing/openrewrite-licensing>)
- <a id="fn-comby-a4"></a>**Comby** no: Syntactic matcher with no data-flow model, "matching and changing coarse syntactic structures". [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-a4"></a>**GritQL** no: Syntactic matching only; no taint mode documented in syntax reference (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/syntax>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-a4"></a>**Coccinelle** no: Intraprocedural only and no taint feature documented; metavariable bindings follow paths within one function. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/main_grammar.html>)

#### A5 Scope of one run {#dim-a5}

- <a id="fn-codespec-a5"></a>**codespec** Whole program: several cir/1 documents, one per package, linked by import path and read as one program including the standard library and dependencies [website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md:81-96](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/static-analysis.md#L81-L96>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-a5"></a>**CodeQL** Per database: one language, whole codebase as built or extracted at one point in time; library code seen only through models. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-overview/about-codeql/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-a5"></a>**Semgrep CE** Per file; taint within one function, constant propagation across functions of one file. "Semgrep CE can only do per-file analysis." [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/glossary>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-a5"></a>**Semgrep Pro** Per file by default (cross-function); whole repository for cross-file mode in supported languages; run only on full scans, not diff-aware. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-code/semgrep-pro-engine-intro>)
- <a id="fn-joern-a5"></a>**Joern** Whole program as imported into one project graph; code imported even when build environment or parts are missing [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-a5"></a>**Infer** Per procedure, over the whole captured project by default; --reactive analyses changed files and their dependencies. Uncaptured library code is an unknown call. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/infer-workflow>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-a5"></a>**SonarQube** Per project, one scanner run; taint is cross-file; C/C++ assumes all analysed files link into one target and cannot see excluded third-party code. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/languages/c-family/customizing-the-analysis>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-a5"></a>**Snyk Code** Whole project, interfile, first-party code: supported files under 4 MB are bundled and sent to Snyk (SaaS); files over 1 MB are skipped. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/snyk-code>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-a5"></a>**Coverity** Whole captured codebase, across files and libraries and their dependencies, per vendor product page; full-project scans. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/static-analysis-tools-sast/coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-a5"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** Whole program including libraries: Android library classes analysed in full; platform JRE chosen with --platform [yanniss.github.io](<https://yanniss.github.io/ptaint-oopsla17-prelim.pdf>)
- <a id="fn-glean-a5"></a>**Glean** One database per indexed repository and revision (name/hash); indexer decides scope; facts de-duplicated across the database [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/databases/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-a5"></a>**SCIP** One Index is one workspace rooted at a directory; cross-repository linking between indexes is left to consumers. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/scip.proto>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-a5"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** Per package (compilation unit), with facts imported from dependencies; multichecker analyses all loaded packages in one process. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-a5"></a>**SpotBugs** One run over a set of class files and jars (project classes); -onlyAnalyze restricts it; auxiliary classpath classes are read but not analysed. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/running.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-a5"></a>**Error Prone** Per compilation unit: runs over attributed compilation units of the javac invocation; dataflow per method. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-a5"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** Per translation unit; cross translation unit analysis is optional, needs an externalDefMap index and an experimental flag. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/user-docs/CrossTranslationUnit.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-a5"></a>**Capslock** Whole program: queried packages plus all their transitive dependencies are loaded and analysed together, results limited to queried packages. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/analyzer/analyzer.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-a5"></a>**ast-grep** Per file: finds files, picks language per extension, matches patterns on each file's syntax tree; files processed in parallel. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/language-injection.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-a5"></a>**OpenRewrite** Whole project per run: LST built in memory from the repository on disk and must fit in memory locally; types read from the classpath. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/lossless-semantic-trees>)
- <a id="fn-comby-a5"></a>**Comby** Per file: patterns are matched file by file (path or stdin) with a language chosen by extension or -matcher. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/get-started>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-a5"></a>**GritQL** Per file by default (patterns auto-wrapped as file(body = contains bubble ...)); multifile steps exist. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/bubble>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-a5"></a>**Coccinelle** Per function control-flow graph within a file; files processed one by one or as groups (--file-groups); optional include processing. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### A6 Third-party dependencies {#dim-a6}

- <a id="fn-codespec-a6"></a>**codespec** partial: Go: scripts/read-repo.sh --deps reads every package go list -deps lists (stdlib and modules) and links them; other languages have no dependency reading (Rust reads one crate) [website/docs/guides/map-a-repository-to-syscalls.md:57-80](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/guides/map-a-repository-to-syscalls.md#L57-L80>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-a6"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Docs: analysis "cannot see inside dependency code"; library behaviour comes from summary, source and sink models as data (beta format). [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/customizing-library-models-for-java-and-kotlin/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-a6"></a>**Semgrep CE** no: Comparison table lists Supply Chain (dependency analysis) as "None" for Community Edition. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-pro-vs-oss>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-a6"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: Supply Chain is a separate product: version matching plus reachability on project code; it "doesn't check the source code of your project's dependencies." [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-supply-chain/overview>)
- <a id="fn-joern-a6"></a>**Joern** partial: Java frontend takes jars only "for type information"; libraries otherwise modelled by data-flow semantics, not analysed from source or bytecode [docs.joern.io](<https://docs.joern.io/frontends/java/>)
- <a id="fn-infer-a6"></a>**Infer** partial: Code Infer cannot see (third-party libraries) is treated as unknown calls with optimistic assumptions; user models via --pulse-model-\* options. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/checker-pulse>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-a6"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Advanced Security (Enterprise and above) extends analysis into open-source dependency code for JS/TS, Java, C#; SCA adds version-based vulnerability matching. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/advanced-security/introduction>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-a6"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Library behaviour comes from framework support trained on projects using them; dependency-tree matching is Snyk Open Source, a separate product. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages-package-managers-and-frameworks/snyk-code-language-support-technical-specifications-and-guidance>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-a6"></a>**Coverity** partial: Product page claims tracking across the codebase and its dependencies; whether dependency source is analysed is not documented on readable pages. [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/static-analysis-tools-sast/coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-a6"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** yes: Library jars given with -i (or Maven coordinates) are analysed with the application; README says pass libraries via -i, not -l [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plast-lab/doop/master/README.md>)
- <a id="fn-glean-a6"></a>**Glean** unknown: The page read does not say it. [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-a6"></a>**SCIP** partial: Symbols carry package manager, name and version; external\_symbols give hover documentation for packages not indexed separately; dependencies are not in one graph. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/scip.proto>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-a6"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** yes: Drivers should cover 'the transitive closure of the packages of interest, including those of the standard library'; facts about dependencies come from their source. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-a6"></a>**SpotBugs** partial: Library classes are read via auxiliary classpath 'but should not themselves be analyzed'; effort max follows calls into referenced classes. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/effort.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-a6"></a>**Error Prone** no: Runs over the compilation units javac compiles; dependencies on the classpath are not analysed. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-a6"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: Library behaviour comes from checker models and annotations (ownership\_returns, ownership\_takes) for code whose definitions it cannot see; sources only if in the TU or CTU. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/user-docs/Annotations.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-a6"></a>**Capslock** yes: Analyses all functions in the packages and their transitive dependencies; third-party dependency capabilities are the stated use case. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/capslock/main/analyzer/analyzer.go>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-a6"></a>**ast-grep** no: Syntax-level tool without scope or type analysis; no dependency graph (harder reading: files are matched one by one). [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/tool-comparison.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-a6"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: Dependency types come from the compilation classpath or TypeTables (serialized type information); dependency bodies are not analysed. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/type-attribution>)
- <a id="fn-comby-a6"></a>**Comby** no: Text-level matcher with no dependency graph; dependencies are analysed only if passed as files, and not linked. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/faq>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-a6"></a>**GritQL** no: Syntactic per-file matcher; no dependency graph documented (harder reading). [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/tutorials/gritql>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-a6"></a>**Coccinelle** no: Included headers are parsed only for type information, not involved in matching and transformation (--include-headers-for-types). [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

## Change

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [C1](#dim-c1) | Diff of two revisions with stable identities | Compares analysis results of two revisions of a program and reports what changed, naming items by identities that survive moved lines. | **yes**: documented. **partial**: partial (for example finding fingerprints, baseline comparison, or a diff-aware scan without a fact diff). **no**: it does not. |
| [C2](#dim-c2) | Code edits | Applies source changes (autofix, codemod, refactoring) driven by a query or pattern. | **yes**: documented. **partial**: only suggested fixes, or limited to some rules. **no**: it does not. |
| [C3](#dim-c3) | Edit verified by re-reading | An edit is checked before it is written, by re-reading or rebuilding the result and comparing it with the expected result. | **yes**: documented. **partial**: syntax re-parse or compile check only, or by running tests. **no**: it does not. |
| [C4](#dim-c4) | Translation between languages | Reads one language and writes another from the same model. | **yes**: documented. **no**: it does not. |
| [C5](#dim-c5) | Behaviour check of a translation | A translation or rewrite is checked by running original and output on the same inputs. | **yes**: documented. **no**: it does not. |

#### C1 Diff of two revisions with stable identities {#dim-c1}

- <a id="fn-codespec-c1"></a>**codespec** planned: codespec diff (functions, signatures, effects, syscalls by call-site id, raises, reach, entries) is built on the open branch wave/release-fact-diff and not on main; main has stable node ids under re-reading only [website/docs/reference/cli.md:181-199](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/wave/release-fact-diff/website/docs/reference/cli.md#L181-L199>) on branch `wave/release-fact-diff`, not on main
- <a id="fn-codeql-c1"></a>**CodeQL** partial: SARIF partialFingerprints (primaryLocationLineHash) identify results across runs; diff-informed analysis filters to changed lines. No fact diff of two revisions. [docs.github.com](<https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli/using-the-advanced-functionality-of-the-codeql-cli/sarif-output>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-c1"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: scan --baseline-commit shows only results not found in that commit; no fact diff; stable fingerprints are platform-only. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/cli-reference>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-c1"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: Diff-aware scans report only findings newly introduced after a baseline; cross-file analysis is skipped in them; no fact diff. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-ci/overview>)

- <a id="fn-infer-c1"></a>**Infer** partial: infer reportdiff compares two issue reports into introduced, fixed and preexisting JSON files; reports issues, not a diff of analysis facts. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/steps-for-ci/>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-c1"></a>**SonarQube** partial: Server tracks issues across analyses by rule, line hash, moved blocks and message (new, existing, fixed). Finding fingerprints, not a fact diff. - <a id="fn-snyk-code-c1"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Pull request checks report new issues per pushed commit and resolve comments when fixed; no fact diff of two revisions. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-fix-and-prevent/prevent/pull-request-checks/pull-request-experience>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-c1"></a>**Coverity** partial: Compares against a baseline so only new issues are reported in pull requests (vendor action, now deprecated). [github.com](<https://github.com/synopsys-sig/coverity-report-output-v7-json>)

#### C2 Code edits {#dim-c2}

- <a id="fn-codespec-c2"></a>**codespec** yes: codespec edit: rename, rename\_field, retarget, delete over Go and Rust, byte-span edits that keep layout; four operations only; dry run by default [website/docs/concepts/code-edits.md:35-47](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/code-edits.md#L35-L47>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-c2"></a>**CodeQL** partial: Only suggested fixes: Autofix generates LLM suggestions inside GitHub code scanning for some queries; not in the open CLI. [docs.github.com](<https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/managing-code-scanning-alerts/about-autofix-for-codeql-code-scanning>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-c2"></a>**Semgrep CE** yes: Rule-defined fix key and fix-regex; --autofix writes changes, --dryrun previews (experimental, "data loss can occur"). [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/autofix>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-c2"></a>**Semgrep Pro** yes: Rule-defined autofix as in CE; Semgrep Multimodal add-on adds suggested fixes and Autofix PRs. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/semgrep-code/overview>)
- <a id="fn-joern-c2"></a>**Joern** no: Scope reading: "platform for analyzing source code, bytecode, and binary executables"; no source-edit feature named (DiffGraph edits the graph only) [github.com](<https://github.com/joernio/joern>)
- <a id="fn-infer-c2"></a>**Infer** no: Documented as a static analyzer that detects and reports bugs; no autofix or codemod feature is documented. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/about-Infer>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-c2"></a>**SonarQube** partial: AI CodeFix proposes edits for selected rules; Enterprise and Data Center only; a suggestion, applied by the developer. [docs.sonarsource.com](<https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/ai-capabilities/ai-codefix>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-c2"></a>**Snyk Code** partial: Snyk Agent Fix suggests fixes, applied in IDE or PR; single-file only, review required. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code/manage-code-vulnerabilities/fix-code-vulnerabilities-automatically>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-c2"></a>**Coverity** unknown: No readable page on applying code edits.
- <a id="fn-doop-c2"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** no: Scope reading: "framework for Java pointer and taint analysis"; no source-edit feature documented [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-c2"></a>**Glean** no: Scope reading: "system for working with facts about source code"; docs suggest building refactoring tools on top, none ships [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-c2"></a>**SCIP** no: Design lists "support use cases involving code modifications" as a non-goal. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-c2"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** yes: Framework decides: diagnostics carry SuggestedFix with TextEdits; unitchecker -fix applies the first fix, -diff prints it. Staticcheck CLI source has no fix flag. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/unitchecker>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-c2"></a>**SpotBugs** no: Scope defined as 'a program to find bugs in Java programs': it reports bug instances and edits no source. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-c2"></a>**Error Prone** yes: Patch mode: -XepPatchChecks picks checks, -XepPatchLocation writes error-prone.patch or IN\_PLACE edits; documented as experimental. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/patching>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-c2"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** yes: clang-tidy -fix applies fixes from checks that provide them; -export-fixes writes YAML for clang-apply-replacements. Analyzer reports only. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-c2"></a>**Capslock** no: Scope is a capability analysis CLI that reports; no code edits or fixes are documented. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-c2"></a>**ast-grep** yes: Rewrite via --rewrite or YAML fix key; applies with --update-all or interactively. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/rewrite-code.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-c2"></a>**OpenRewrite** yes: Recipes change the LST and print it back preserving formatting; Maven rewrite:run and Gradle rewriteRun write the edits. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/lossless-semantic-trees>)
- <a id="fn-comby-c2"></a>**Comby** yes: Core purpose: match templates rewritten by rewrite templates, in place (-i) or as diff; interactive -review. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/basic-usage>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-c2"></a>**GritQL** yes: Rewrites with =\> in patterns; grit apply, grit check --fix. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/cli/reference>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-c2"></a>**Coccinelle** yes: Semantic patches transform C code; output is a unified diff, or --in-place, -o, --out-place. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### C3 Edit verified by re-reading {#dim-c3}

- <a id="fn-codespec-c3"></a>**codespec** yes: Before output the edited copy is read again and must equal the expected cir/1 byte for byte; --build adds go build/vet or cargo check; --apply checks SHA-256 and rolls back on failure [website/docs/concepts/code-edits.md:78-94](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/website/docs/concepts/code-edits.md#L78-L94>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-c3"></a>**CodeQL** unknown: No source found for verification of an edit.
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-c3"></a>**Semgrep CE** partial: No pre-write check on user code; semgrep --test applies a rule's fix to a test file and compares with a .fixed file. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/testing-rules>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-c3"></a>**Semgrep Pro** partial: No pre-write check on user code; semgrep --test compares a rule's fix output with a .fixed file. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/testing-rules>)
- <a id="fn-joern-c3"></a>**Joern** no: Same scope reading as C2: analysis platform, no source edits to verify [github.com](<https://github.com/joernio/joern>)
- <a id="fn-infer-c3"></a>**Infer** no: Scope is bug reporting; no edit is made, so none is verified (harder reading, see C2). [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/about-Infer>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-c3"></a>**SonarQube** unknown: AI CodeFix page describes no check of the proposed edit.
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-c3"></a>**Snyk Code** yes: Static analysis engine re-checks each candidate fix for vulnerability gone and none introduced; failing candidates are retried or withheld. [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code/manage-code-vulnerabilities/fix-code-vulnerabilities-automatically>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-c3"></a>**Coverity** unknown: No readable page on verifying edits.
- <a id="fn-doop-c3"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** no: Same scope reading as C2: analysis framework, no edits to verify [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-c3"></a>**Glean** no: Same scope reading as C2: no edits to verify [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-c3"></a>**SCIP** no: Code modification is a stated non-goal, so no edits are made or verified. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-c3"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** partial: analysistest.RunWithSuggestedFixes applies fixes and verifies output against golden files, at test time only; the driver is not documented to re-check before writing. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/analysistest>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-c3"></a>**SpotBugs** no: No edits are made (C2); the tool only reports bugs. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-c3"></a>**Error Prone** partial: BugCheckerRefactoringTestHelper compares a transformed file with expected source at test time; patching page does not say patched code is rebuilt. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/package-summary.html>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-c3"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** partial: Check tests run a second FileCheck pass (CHECK-FIXES) on fixed code at test time; docs do not say fixed output is recompiled. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/Contributing.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-c3"></a>**Capslock** no: Scope is reporting capabilities; it writes no edits, so none are verified. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-c3"></a>**ast-grep** no: Rewrite is text substitution on matched node; page warns result may not be valid code; no verification step documented. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/rewrite-code.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-c3"></a>**OpenRewrite** partial: RewriteTest compares recipe output with expected "after" source and flags missing types; runtime edits are not re-verified (compile check is a Moderne feature). [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/authoring-recipes/recipe-testing>)
- <a id="fn-comby-c3"></a>**Comby** unknown: Pages read describe no check of the rewritten output; FAQ suggests running a formatter afterwards.
- <a id="fn-gritql-c3"></a>**GritQL** partial: Rewrite output is validity-checked by default; the raw form skips checks and may emit invalid code. No re-read comparison documented. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/patterns>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-c3"></a>**Coccinelle** partial: Test harness (--ctestall, --compare-with-expected) compares results with expected .res files; no re-read check of each edit documented. [coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr](<https://coccinelle.gitlabpages.inria.fr/website/docs/options.pdf>)

#### C4 Translation between languages {#dim-c4}

- <a id="fn-codespec-c4"></a>**codespec** yes: Go to Rust and Rust to Go (examples), also C, Elixir, Gleam, Odin writers; each reader and writer reads a subset only (Elixir, Gleam and Odin typed scalar functions) [README.md:3-5](<https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/70c6c4ebc42c/README.md#L3-L5>)
- <a id="fn-codeql-c4"></a>**CodeQL** no: Scope is analysis: queries select results from an extracted database; no code writer documented. Page defines queries as examining code for problems. [codeql.github.com](<https://codeql.github.com/docs/writing-codeql-queries/about-codeql-queries/>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-ce-c4"></a>**Semgrep CE** no: Scope: fix replaces matched metavariables and regex matches in place; no cross-language writer documented. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/autofix>)
- <a id="fn-semgrep-pro-c4"></a>**Semgrep Pro** no: Scope: fix replaces matched metavariables and regex matches in place; no cross-language writer documented. [docs.semgrep.dev](<https://docs.semgrep.dev/writing-rules/autofix>)
- <a id="fn-joern-c4"></a>**Joern** no: Same scope reading as C2: reads many languages into a graph, no code writing documented [github.com](<https://github.com/joernio/joern>)
- <a id="fn-infer-c4"></a>**Infer** no: Scope is analysis of Java, C, C++, Objective-C and Erlang for bugs; no code generation in another language is documented. [fbinfer.com](<https://fbinfer.com/docs/about-Infer>)
- <a id="fn-sonarqube-c4"></a>**SonarQube** no: Repository defines the product as a code analysis platform; no translation feature (structural scope, none documented). [github.com](<https://github.com/SonarSource/sonarqube>)
- <a id="fn-snyk-code-c4"></a>**Snyk Code** no: Defined as a SAST solution; no translation between languages (structural scope). [docs.snyk.io](<https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/snyk-code>)
- <a id="fn-coverity-c4"></a>**Coverity** no: Product scans source code without executing it and finds defects; no translation between languages (structural scope). [www.blackduck.com](<https://www.blackduck.com/static-analysis-tools-sast/coverity.html>)
- <a id="fn-doop-c4"></a>**Doop (Soufflé)** no: Same scope reading as C2: no code writing from the model documented [github.com](<https://github.com/plast-lab/doop>)
- <a id="fn-glean-c4"></a>**Glean** no: Same scope reading as C2: no code writing documented [glean.software](<https://glean.software/docs/introduction/>)
- <a id="fn-scip-c4"></a>**SCIP** no: Code modification and generation are a non-goal; protocol only describes indexed source. [raw.githubusercontent.com](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sourcegraph/scip/main/docs/DESIGN.md>)
- <a id="fn-go-analysis-c4"></a>**staticcheck / go/analysis** no: Fixes are TextEdits on the analysed package's own Go files; no translation to another language is part of the framework. [pkg.go.dev](<https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis>)
- <a id="fn-spotbugs-c4"></a>**SpotBugs** no: Scope is finding bugs in Java bytecode; no output language. [spotbugs.readthedocs.io](<https://spotbugs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html>)
- <a id="fn-errorprone-c4"></a>**Error Prone** no: Patches and Refaster templates rewrite Java source in place; no output language. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/refaster>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-c4"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** no: Fix-its edit the same C/C++ source in place; no output language is part of the tool. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-c4"></a>**Capslock** no: Scope is capability analysis of Go packages; no translation to another language. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-c4"></a>**ast-grep** no: Rewrite replaces node text within one language; a rule targets a single language, no cross-language model. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/faq.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-c4"></a>**OpenRewrite** no: Model is modify the LST and print it back into source of the same language. [docs.openrewrite.org](<https://docs.openrewrite.org/>)
- <a id="fn-comby-c4"></a>**Comby** no: Rewrite replaces matched text in place within the same file; no model to write another language from. [comby.dev](<https://comby.dev/docs/basic-usage>)
- <a id="fn-gritql-c4"></a>**GritQL** no: A pattern file declares one target language and rewrites emit that language. [docs.grit.io](<https://docs.grit.io/language/target-languages>)
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-c4"></a>**Coccinelle** no: README: style-preserving source-to-source transformations on C source code; Rust is a separate tool. [github.com](<https://github.com/coccinelle/coccinelle>)

- <a id="fn-errorprone-c5"></a>**Error Prone** no: No translation exists (C4); Refaster rewrites Java to Java and docs describe no run comparison. [errorprone.info](<https://errorprone.info/docs/refaster>)
- <a id="fn-clang-sa-c5"></a>**Clang SA / tidy** no: No translation exists (C4); fixes are text edits checked only by FileCheck patterns at test time. [clang.llvm.org](<https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/Contributing.html>)
- <a id="fn-capslock-c5"></a>**Capslock** no: Scope is capability analysis of Go packages; no translation or rewrite is produced. [github.com](<https://github.com/google/capslock>)
- <a id="fn-ast-grep-c5"></a>**ast-grep** no: Works purely at syntax level, no execution of code; fix is text substitution. [ast-grep.github.io](<https://ast-grep.github.io/advanced/tool-comparison.html>)
- <a id="fn-openrewrite-c5"></a>**OpenRewrite** unknown: No behaviour comparison of original and output documented in pages read.
- <a id="fn-comby-c5"></a>**Comby** unknown: No behaviour comparison of original and rewritten code documented in pages read.
- <a id="fn-gritql-c5"></a>**GritQL** unknown: No behaviour comparison of original and rewritten code documented.
- <a id="fn-coccinelle-c5"></a>**Coccinelle** unknown: No behaviour comparison of original and transformed code documented.

## Ecosystem

### Dimensions

| id | dimension | question | how a cell is decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| [E1](#dim-e1) | Conformance kit for third-party adapters | A published test kit lets an outside author check a front end or adapter against a feature list. | **yes**: documented kit with per-feature verdicts. **partial**: a testing guide or harness without a feature vocabulary. **no**: it does not. |
| [E2](#dim-e2) | Documented determinism | Documentation states that the same input gives byte-identical output (or tests it). | **yes**: stated or tested. **partial**: stated for part of the output. **no**: not stated. |
| [E3](#dim-e3) | Licence | The licence of the engine and, where different, of the rules or query libraries. Cell text: the licence. | text, not a verdict |
| [E4](#dim-e4) | Self-hosted and offline | Runs on the user's own machine or infrastructure without sending code to a vendor service. | **yes**: it does. **partial**: yes for the engine but a paid tier or cloud is needed for some features. **no**: cloud only. |
| [E5](#dim-e5) | CI integration | Documented way to run in CI (official action, plugin or CI guide). | **yes**: it does. **partial**: command line only. **no**: it does not. |
| [E6](#dim-e6) | Output formats | Machine-readable result formats the tool documents (SARIF, JSON, XML, CSV, other). Cell text: the list. | text, not a verdict |
| [E7](#dim-e7) | Ships a maintained rule catalogue | The project or vendor ships and maintains ready-made rules or queries. | **yes**: it does. **partial**: examples only. **no**: it does not. |
